  "text": "At closing time, Ellen found her brother kneeling beside the shop counter, peeling tape from an extension lead.

“You can leave that,” she said.

“It’s ours.”

“So is the dust. We’re leaving that.”

Paul wound the cable around his elbow. Where the till had stood, the wood was pale and unmarked.

“Did she come for the sewing machine?”

“Her husband did.”

“Did you give him the pedal?”

“It was in the case.”

Outside, a bus stopped. For a moment the windows filled with faces, then cleared again.

Ellen checked the drawers. Buttons, a bent paperclip, the little notebook their mother had used for alterations.

“What about this?”

Paul got up slowly.

“Anyone still owe anything?”

“Mrs Bell. Four pounds.”

“She died.”

“I know.”

Ellen flicked through the pages. Their mother’s handwriting grew larger towards the back. On the last page was a shopping list: milk, pears, batteries.

Paul held out his hand, but when she offered the notebook he reached past it for the drawer.

“It catches,” he said. “You have to lift.”

She lifted. The drawer slid home.

The landlord would arrive at six. Ellen put the keys on the counter, then picked them up again.

“We should take the sign out of the window.”

Paul unhooked it. CLOSED, in red letters, with a small clock beneath. Their mother had set the hands to nine and never changed them.

“Bin?” he asked.

Ellen opened her bag.

He turned the clock hands flat before putting it inside, so they wouldn’t catch on anything."
